correctness.rationale: The primary Definition 6.1 was read in full text. In a finite sigma-field the sigma-ideal is principal, generated by the union Z of all null sets. Modal ideal closure forbids a surviving atom from reaching a null atom. If one surviving atom reached two distinct surviving atoms Q0,Q1, applying the marked countable-intersection condition to Q0,Q1,X,X,... would put a non-null atom in an intersection that must be null, a contradiction. Thus the surviving atom relation is partial-functional. The quotient map to subsets of surviving atoms is a Boolean isomorphism and intertwines diamond with inverse image. Conversely a finite partial function satisfies the marked intersection condition. On finite atomic Boolean algebras, additivity plus meet preservation is exactly the same at-most-one-successor condition. The frozen exhaustive checker was read and corroborates the structural equivalence on one through three atoms.
correctness.risk: The collapse is essentially finite/atomic; it does not extend directly to infinite sigma-fields.

value.rationale: The theorem sharply separates finite from merely measurable representability, reduces finite marked semantics to deterministic partial dynamics, gives a simple algebraic test, and identifies the smallest obstruction. These are natural structural consequences for a new representation semantics.
value.risk: The finite collapse does not address cardinal bounds for infinite representations.

final_claim: Every finite marked modal measurable quotient is exactly the complex algebra of a partial function on its non-null Boolean atoms; equivalently, a finite modal Boolean algebra has such a finite representation exactly when its normal additive diamond also preserves binary meets. The four-element branching algebra is the smallest finite algebra requiring an infinite marked-modal-measurable representation.
limitations: Finite underlying measurable spaces and finite quotient algebras only.
No cardinality classification of infinite representations is claimed.
